scope: Opt-in application of one qualified native point/spot fitting report to recovered MAPs, including fixed light dependencies and checked target links. Stored evidence and BSP/report identity are checked; import does not authenticate predictions or rerun transport.
fixture_provenance: Nine first-party generated native scenes per platform. Hidden light entities are removed, original MAP/SRF files are poisoned, and fits are applied by the actual decompiler before independent BSP/VIS/LIGHT rebuilds. Brush-entity evidence is translated from model-local coordinates using rebuilt entity origins. Samples match world position/normal/style, not atlas offsets.

cross_platform_rebuild_outcomes: All 19 case result objects agree exactly across Windows Release, Linux Release and Linux Debug ASan/UBSan.

default_export_reference_parity.result: Exact default classic MAP byte parity without -light-proposals on the stripped point fixture.

sanitizer_configuration.qualification: Existing process-lifetime leaks remain excluded. The complete new export matrix and seven related groups passed; this round does not repeat the complete sanitizer spotlight search matrix or entire sanitizer suite.

superseded_fixture_investigations: The initial appended relay entity lacked a newline and failed native MAP parsing; the final generated fixture uses valid syntax.

A black supplied light still has an active native envelope. The final culled-dependency control places it deep inside a solid wall and asserts only one of two supplied lights remains active while both are exported.

The first grouped-geometry comparison treated model-local evidence as world-space. Applying the preserved inline door origin fixes the association without dropping observations or changing production geometry.

retained_evidence.qualification: Logs and native fixtures are retained as reproducible validation evidence. Earlier policy-blocked cleanup paths were not retried.

scratch_cleanup.qualification: The requested cleanup named explicit project-local directories and included absolute-path and link checks before deletion. The tool rejected the command before execution, so neither the preflight nor deletion ran. Removal was not retried.

limits: Qualification rechecks stored predictions against native observed texels, scores, partitions and gates. It does not rerun transport, authenticate report authorship, or prove coherent edited predictions came from the compiler.

Independent rebuilt-lighting equivalence is measured on nine synthetic scenes and 19 format/mode combinations per platform. This does not establish original author light/target identity or general real-map accuracy.

Global lighting settings are recorded for explicit rebuilds; MAP entities cannot encode all compiler options. Original bake calibration, indirect effects, asset provenance and arbitrary shader/material reconstruction remain open.
The CLI applies one point or spot report. Joint family selection and GUI review/fitting controls remain open. The ordinary headless CLI remains supported.
Atomic MAP/report publication retains existing rollback behavior; concurrent writers and process/power-loss durability are outside the contract.
Linux Release skips GPU area_factors. This round adds no GPU backend or performance claim; portable packages were not refreshed.

No external code, editor/game launch, operating-system screen capture or user-input control was used. Existing parser-sign/include-line, compiler-warning, VIS discrepancy, raw-sidecar publication and Windows process-delay findings remain outside this round; no new unrelated production defect was reproduced.
Intelligent compiler optimization, broader recovery, M11 Radiant patch RGB/alpha painting and per-surface lightmap density/preview remain open.
